 THIS M.F.A. IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
 1988 AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.12.2016  PASSED IN MVC NO.151/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE MEMBER MOTOR  ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNALS-II, BAGALKOT, PARTLY ALLOWING  THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING  ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:3412  MFA No. 101953 of 2017  JUDGMENT Heard Sri.D.V.Pattar, learned counsel for the appellant and Miss.Vinaya Kuppelur on behalf of Sri.S.S.Koliwad, learned counsel for respondent - Insurance Company.
2.
Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

3. This is claimant's appeal challenging the validity of judgment and award passed in MVC No.151/2013 on the file of Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bagalkot dated 05.12.2016 on the ground of shifting liability on the Insurance Company and also on the ground of inadequacy of compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bagalkot
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of this case are as under:
5. Claimant laid a claim under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for the accidental injuries sustained by him on 04.04.2012 at about 11:30 p.m. being pillion rider NC: 2024:KHC-D:3412 of motorcycle bearing No.KA-29/F-9116 and three wheeler goods vehicle bearing No.KA-26/6553.
He was shifted to hospital and cured of all injuries.
6. In respect of accident, police filed charge sheet against the driver of goods vehicle.

7. Tribunal, on contest, allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.2,63,905/- as compensation payable by the owner of Auto rickshaw on the ground that driver of the vehicle did not have proper endorsement to drive the goods vehicle though he had licence to drive a light motor vehicle.

sentences.text: 2 8. Being aggrieved by the said judgment, claimant is in appeal.
9. Sri
. D.V.Pattar, learned counsel for the appellant contended that award of compensation is on lower side and sought for reasonable enhancement.

10. He also contended that liability fastened on the owner is incorrect in view of the principles of law NC: 2024:KHC-D:3412 enunciated in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668.
11.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel representing Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment.
12. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

13. On such perusal of material on record, it is crystal clear that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 04.04.2012 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-29/F-9116 and three wheeler goods vehicle bearing No.KA-26/6553.
14.

Taking note of award of compensation in a sum of Rs.2,63,905/- by the Tribunal, this Court is of the considered opinion that compensation awarded is just and sufficient for the injuries sustained by the claimant and there is no scope for enhancement of compensation NC: 2024:KHC-D:3412 inasmuch as on all heads award of compensation is just an proper.
15. Insofar as liability is concerned, in view of authoritative principles of law enunciated in Mukund Dewangan, supra Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation and not the owner of vehicle.

16. Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) While maintaining the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
claimant is entitled to receive Rs.2,63,905/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation from the Insurance Company of goods vehicle who is respondent No.2 in this appeal.
(iii) Six weeks time is granted for the Insurance Company to deposit compensation amount before the Tribunal.

Sd/-
